principles: Show what happened — every event in process-events.jsonl maps to at least one visible node
Show what is planned — checklist items with verificationIntent are visible even before dispatch
Graceful degradation — early-phase stories show fewer nodes but never zero or a crash
No mutation — serve.js and lineage.js are read-only observers of Lattice state files
Correct emptiness — never show LLM call sections when the count is zero
drivers: All dashboard files are outside the Orchestrate repo; changes go directly to /Users/jek/Documents/
Server must restart to pick up serve.js changes (node module cache); lineage.js and demo.html hot-reload
verificationIntent in checklist.json and codex_cli events are the only available LLM content proxies — no raw prompt/response is stored

options.name: add-understanding-and-pending-nodes
pros: PLAN-phase stories show meaningful plan-layer node with task/outcome from understanding.json
DEV-phase stories show CHK items even before dispatch — LLM intent visible pre-agent-run
Complete picture for any lifecycle stage
cons: Two new code paths to maintain in serve.js
Pending nodes could confuse reviewers if they look similar to real dispatch nodes

options.name: verify-only-no-new-nodes
pros: Zero code risk — existing implementation might already satisfy the user
cons: PLAN-phase stories still show no plan-layer artifact — understanding.json ignored
DEV stories with no dispatches show only INIT-review nodes which are not labelled clearly
User asked for complete lifecycle — empty plan layer for PLAN stories is incomplete

rationale: The user explicitly asked for 'complete lifecycle' for every story phase. Without adding understanding node and pending-CHK nodes, a PLAN-phase story shows no plan-layer evidence and a DEV-phase story shows no CHK nodes until dispatch happens. Both gaps misrepresent the story state.

preMortem.trigger: Story just entered PLAN before understanding_set was called
preMortem.mitigation: Guard with existsSync and optional chaining; only create node if understanding.json has a task field

preMortem.scenario: pending-dispatch nodes confuse user — look identical to real dispatch nodes
preMortem.trigger: User clicks a pending node expecting LLM trace data
preMortem.consequence: Panel shows verificationIntent but no codexCalls or durationMs — could be misleading
preMortem.mitigation: Use kind=pending-agent and show sub label as pending — not dispatched yet, so panel omits duration/codexOps fields

preMortem.scenario: serve.js edit does not take effect (module cache)
preMortem.trigger: Developer edits serve.js but forgets to restart server
preMortem.mitigation: Always restart server via preview_start or pkill after serve.js edits
